With 5 players, put 4 favor in each suit bank. People’s Favor starts normal with 1 favor; Darkest Secret starts with 1 secret. Chancellor starts with 2 favor, 1 secret, and 3 purple warbands on board. Each Exile or Citizen starts with 1 favor and 1 secret; Exiles have 3 own-color warbands on board, Citizens 3 purple. All have full leftmost Supply.
Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)

Deal saved sites and attached cards to map slots in Cradle, then Provinces, then Hinterland, each top to bottom. Chancellor places 2 purple warbands on topmost faceup Cradle site and 1 at each other faceup site with a denizen or intact edifice. Resolve printed favor/secret setup prompts on sites from shared bank; if favor is insufficient, Chancellor chooses allocation. Existing Chronicled relics stay at sites.
Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)

Players may choose an Exile or Citizen board on its saved side; Citizens do not receive a Reliquary relic in setup. Chancellor starts holding Oathkeeper title; additionally takes Darkest Secret for Devotion or People’s Favor for People. Starting Citizens get no banner from that clause. Chancellor is chosen by any method (previous winner recommended, not required).
Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)

If required, rebuild world deck first as 10 denizens + 2 random Visions, next 15 denizens + remaining 3 Visions, then remaining denizens. Take 3 cards from bottom, one per region discard. Each player in turn order draws 3 from bottom and advances Visions Drawn for any Visions drawn. Each chooses 1 as facedown adviser and discards 2 to normal regional destinations. Then place remaining deck on map. Reliquary gets 4 relics drawn and placed randomly, one facedown per space; rest form relic deck.
Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)

First game: Plains/Mountain/Rocky Coast start faceup (top Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland); other five packet sites are facedown in marked order. Purple pawn is on Plains, Red/Blue on Mountain, Yellow on Rocky Coast; garrisons are 2 purple Plains, 1 purple Mountain and Rocky Coast. Longbows/Taming Charm/Elders go on those respective sites. Starting facedown advisers: Chancellor Forest Paths, Red Animal Playmates, Blue Naysayers, Yellow A Small Favor. Ivory Eye is facedown at Mountain; next four packet relics are facedown on Reliquary spaces.
First game: preserve the packet order

Muster and Trade require an eligible empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn’s site; remote rule does not permit either. Ordinary Action powers are available if you rule the card or your pawn is at its site (relic holder can use held relics); sites state their own conditions. Campaign battle plans at a site require that you rule it, not just pawn presence. Persistent powers (thick black braid) affect their specified players regardless of ordinary access.
Muster — 1 Supply|Trade — 1 Supply|Powers, costs and information|Campaign — 2 Supply

When paid outside your turn, favor goes immediately to its matching bank; secrets go facedown on your board and cannot pay another cost until flipped faceup. A battle plan may be paid even if the card already holds resources, but it remains usable only once per Campaign.

Ordinary major-action modifiers are chosen at action start and used once per action, in any order; the same no-cost modifier may be used on multiple distinct actions, but not twice on one action. Do not discard an active modifier during that action. Must/cannot modifiers are mandatory.

When Played effects resolve after normal site-play favor and Homeland reward. Ordinary Wake powers happen once during Wake and must resolve as much as possible; only “may” parts are optional. Rest powers are optional once each at end of Rest. A paid power may be used even if its effect does nothing; resolve as much as possible, preserving optional “may” choices.
Powers, costs and information|Site powers (Site Reference)

Faceup tree cards are site-only; person cards are adviser-only; follow those placement limits when playing, moving or swapping, plus capacity and locked-card restrictions. Locked faceup cards cannot be discarded, moved or swapped except in Chronicle. Facedown cards have no restrictions. When reducing adviser limit, discard to the new limit before playing; with multiple limit changers use the lowest, not their sum.

Anyone may play Conspiracy faceup; it does not replace a true Vision. Burn 1 secret to take a relic or banner from a player whose pawn is at your site (including another Imperial) only if at least 2 of your faceup advisers match the suit of any of their advisers. Both of yours can match one of theirs. Apply banner seizure penalty, then return Conspiracy to the box even if no theft occurred.

A faceup adviser cannot be freely discarded; it leaves only when another rule permits/requires it, respecting locks. Minor action: move any number of your warbands from your site to board except the last one; drop board warbands at your site only if you rule it, so you cannot drop onto an empty bandit site. Citizen pickup requires Chancellor permission. Imperial players with pawns together may give/take board warbands from one another with recipient/other player permission.
Adviser retention depends on its state|Minor actions — no Supply

You may peek at facedown relics at your site without Supply. Once you have peeked at a particular relic, you may peek at it again from any site. Grand Scepter holder may use its power to peek in Reliquary, but cannot use either Scepter power on the turn they took it.

Scepter holder exiling another Citizen pays them 5 favor, +1 if recipient is Oathkeeper, +1 if recipient holds People’s Favor, −1 if payer is Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People’s Favor (range 3–7). Recipient flips to Exile, replaces board purple warbands with own color, refreshes full Supply; purple map garrisons stay Imperial. This action does not end their Act by itself.

A Citizen without the Scepter may self-exile by giving its holder favor equal to own board warbands plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards. A Scepter holder cannot self-exile. Then flip Exile, replace own board warbands with own color, refresh full Supply, and end Act. Purple map garrisons stay Imperial.

A current titleholder keeps title on a tie. If the holder falls behind and multiple others tie for the goal, the outgoing holder chooses the recipient. Supremacy transfers at end of Campaign, not while temporary loss of site rule is being resolved.
Title transfer and victory timing|Campaign — 2 Supply

given_state: The current holder first ties another player, then later falls behind two tied leaders.
completed_events: The first tie preserves the incumbent title. In the later state the holder no longer meets the goal and two others tie.
next_operation: Transfer the title at its normal timing; on that tie the outgoing holder chooses either tied leader.
result: The original holder keeps it during the tie and chooses the recipient after falling behind; Supremacy title transfer waits until Campaign end.

Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans first, then defender; bandits use all plans at sites they rule, without cost. Red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either; rule alone cannot waive the color restriction. If a plan removes an attack die from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.

Casualty bookkeeping: skull losses happen once when rolled. If five warbands are described as remaining after skulls and the attacker loses, defeat kills floor(5/2)=2 and leaves 3 on the attacker’s board. A victorious defender does not gain attacker’s declared targets; only attacker victory resolves targets.

given_state: Five attacking force warbands remain after skull casualties; attacker loses.
completed_events: Skull casualties have already been removed and the battle is lost.
next_operation: Apply defeat loss to the remaining force: floor(5/2)=2 killed; 5−2=3 survivors.
result: Three stay on attacker’s board. A winning defender does not take attacker relics.

Defender board force counts only if the defender’s pawn is at the attacker’s site or one of the targeted sites. Warbands at untargeted sites do not defend. Shields are counted after doubling shield rolls for each double-symbol; multipliers stack, and doubles affect shields only, not warbands.

Favor, warbands, and cards are component-limited; take/gain as much as possible if a source is short. Secrets and dice are unlimited (multipliers or reroll as needed). You cannot give away, burn, or sacrifice extra resources beyond the instructed cost or amount.
